title: Rafael and the Compass
premise: Elodie Ashgrove, a courier carrying sealed diplomatic codes for a republic on the brink of collapse, has spent years perfecting the art of being overlooked. When one dispatch names his own family as conspirators in a plot to betray the state, he must choose between burning the letter and preserving himself, or delivering it and dooming everyone he loves. Racing against the republic's fall and the victors' historians who will write its epitaph, Elodie smuggles the truth into an archive that will outlast both sides. He survives the century's turn not as a hero or a traitor, but as the quiet man who made sure the record could not be quietly rewritten.
about_author: Sebastian Zhou is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing the private papers of failed states. He writes historical fiction from the margins of official records, where the truth usually hides in plain sight.

chapters.title: The Weight of Sealed Things
chapters.summary: In Elodie's POV, we follow his final courier run through a capital gripped by rumor and ration lines, establishing his craft of invisibility and his careful distance from his estranged family. When he seals the last dispatch pouch, he notices one letter bears his family's name among the accused. The emotional beat is dread disguised as routine: the moment invisibility becomes complicity.

chapters.title: What the Ashgroves Kept
chapters.summary: Alternating between Elodie's present flight and his sister Marguerite's POV at the family estate, this chapter reveals the inheritance at stake: not land, but a ledger of old debts that implicates them all. Elodie arrives seeking answers and finds soldiers arriving first. The emotional beat is the collision of love and duty, as siblings who barely speak must now decide together what to protect.

chapters.title: The Historians Are Coming
chapters.summary: With the republic falling street by street, Elodie races a victor's commission already drafting the official history, using his courier credentials to slip past checkpoints with the letter and the ledger. A betrayal by his handler forces him to burn his own cover identity. The climax lands in the archive itself, where Elodie must hide the truth in plain sight before the doors are sealed.

chapters.title: On the Record
chapters.summary: Years later, in Elodie's aged POV, a young historian uncovers the misfiled documents he planted, and he must decide whether to claim authorship of the truth or let it stand anonymous. He chooses the record over recognition, telling her only enough to verify it. The resolution offers quiet redemption: identity surrendered so that truth, and family memory, survive the century's turn.
